plans.note: Section 21 has a mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, a consequential-damages waiver with direct-damage clarifications, and Excluded Claims for confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud and IP. Check carve-outs and that our payment obligation is unlimited (21.3). Cross-check insurance non-limitation in 18.2.

Vendor IP indemnity (20.1), broader misconduct/data/law indemnity (20.2), narrow reciprocal Customer indemnity (20.3), procedure (20.4) and infringement remedies with refund (20.5). Confirm Customer indemnity stays limited to unmodified Customer material and unlawful use, and that indemnities are Excluded Claims under 21.3.

Section 12.3 expressly preserves our freedom to develop, buy, or compete and disclaims non-compete/MFC/volume/no-hire commitments. Check for any conflicting restriction elsewhere (2.2 exclusivity, 12.4 no-hire) before concluding compliance under this rule; exclusivity is handled under EXCLUSIVITY.

Section 2.2 (first of two 2.2s) makes Vendor our sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the term — a direct breach; note the conflict with 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and 12.3 (no exclusivity acknowledged).

Section 7.2 (first of two 7.2s) obliges Customer to give Vendor terms no less favourable than any other technology supplier — an MFN running against us, contradicted by 12.3's disclaimer of most-favoured-customer commitments.

Section 12.4 binds Customer for eighteen months post-termination, covers any person employed at any time during the term, bars engagement as well as solicitation, and has no general-advertising carve-out; contrast 12.3's general-recruitment freedom.

Section 9 contains only for-cause, insolvency and Customer-specific cause triggers plus force-majeure exit in 27.3; no general termination-for-convenience right for Customer appears — verify against 8.1/8.2 term and 10.2 refund mechanics before marking missing.

Section 8.2 auto-renews Order Forms for twelve months on a 180-day non-renewal notice — an onerous window; 8.3 caps uplift at lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice, which is favourable and should be noted, not flagged.
New York law with New York County courts and a pre-suit executive escalation that preserves urgent relief; confirm no foreign arbitration is imported elsewhere.

24.1 gives us free affiliate/successor assignment, 24.2 restricts Vendor, 24.4 blocks Vendor termination or repricing on our change of control; 13.3 allows transfer of licence rights. Check 24.3's residual mutual consent for consistency.

Customer owns Customer Data and Deliverables with assignment (14.1–14.2); Vendor retains Vendor Technology with a perpetual licence back via 13.2/14.3; feedback and joint-IP handled in 14.4. Confirm the payment condition in 14.2 and the data-use restrictions in 15.1 (no model training).

13.1 covers Affiliates and contractors worldwide; 13.2 grants a perpetual paid-up licence for delivered technology; 13.3 limits revocation/suspension to material uncured breach after cure opportunity. Review 13.4 restrictions for over-breadth.

Section 22.1 permits Vendor audits at any time without notice with remote system access — a clear breach; 22.2 and 22.3 provide cost allocation, scope limits and confidentiality that partly mitigate. Section 23 (Records and Customer Assurance) may also bear on records access.
Section 7.6 imposes USD 25,000/day liquidated damages on Customer for dependency delays; consider interaction with the liability cap in 21.1 and the absence of any reciprocal service-credit regime.

Ninety-day Deliverable warranty plus term-long hosted conformance (19.2), malicious-code and compliance warranties (19.3), repair/re-perform with refund fallback and non-exclusive remedy (19.4); disclaimer in 19.5 preserves express warranties. Acceptance remedies in 6.1–6.2 are related.
Section 18.1 sets CGL, workers' comp, employer's liability, E&O and USD 5M cyber cover for the term plus one year; 18.2 covers certificates, primacy and non-limitation of liability.

Section 2.1 expressly disclaims minimum quantity or purchase commitments and 12.3 confirms no minimum-volume commitment; check 7.1's bar on minimum-use charges. Likely compliant unless an exclusivity-driven de facto commitment (2.2) is read as volume lock-in.

Section 11 provides up to six months' transition assistance at expiring rates, 30-day data return in machine-readable format with no fee-dispute hostage, and certified deletion; 10.1–10.2 cover post-termination rights and refunds.
